title: Corrections to Numerical Optimization, Second Edition (last updated May 17, 2008): errata list from Wright's homepage
contribution: Wright's copy of the joint second-edition errata (May 17, 2008; 79 items). It is identical to Nocedal's copy B003 (May 27, 2008; 80 items) except that it lacks B003's item 12 (book p. 63, a paragraph removed), so B004 items 12-79 are B003 items 13-80. Internet Archive digests show both copies unchanged since 2008 (Wright's live file identical on 2026-10-17), so the list stopped in May 2008 and the copies were never reconciled. Nocedal's SKILL counts 80 (B003); Wright's skill counts 79 (B004).
problem_entry: Read for its differences from B003 only (works.json note). The same joint list as B003, hosted by Wright (live listing: NumOpt2-typos.pdf and NumOpt2-typos.tex dated 2008-05-17 12:10). It matters because Nocedal's SKILL.md Heuristic 7 and 03 §4.3 count 80 items (B003), while Wright's 03-process-evidence §2.1 counts 79 (this copy) (pp. 1, 5).
key_idea: Differences from B003: header '(Last updated May 17, 2008)' against May 27 (p. 1); 79 items against 80; B003's item 12 (book p. 63, line 8: remove the paragraph from 'Another strategy' to 'Goldfarb [132])') is absent, so items 1-11 match and items 12-79 equal B003 items 13-80; the acknowledgement is identical (p. 5). Five items (22, 23, 33, 34, 67; pp. 2, 3, 5) differ only in where the text layer places bar and hat accents. Book p. 63 holds the end of Chapter 3's Notes and References and the start of its Exercises [B001 p. 8]; that the paragraph is in the Notes is an inference. It is the only item in either copy that removes a whole paragraph without replacement; the other deletions remove phrases (items 13, 26, 40; pp. 1-3).
assumptions: n/a for this card: no hypothesis-level item differs between the copies.
proof_devices: n/a for this card: the one proof repair (implicit-function argument for book p. 325) is in both copies (B004 item 52, p. 4 = B003 item 53, B003 p. 4).
positioning: The same three readers are thanked, with no item attributed to a finder (p. 5). Neither copy mentions the other.
writing: Format identical to B003's: book page and line (negative lines counted from the bottom), printed text and replacement joined by an arrow, 'should be' or 'Replace ... by' for formulas (pp. 1-5). No version line or changelog, so a reader of either copy cannot tell that a second, different copy exists.
limits_future: Both copies are frozen: Wright's file has one SHA-1 digest from its first Internet Archive capture (2008-10-31) to 2024-08-22, equal to the local B004, and the live file was identical on 2026-10-17; Nocedal's errata2.pdf has one digest from 2008-07-25 to 2024-07-19, equal to B003 (my CDX and hash check). No update after May 27, 2008 is visible on either host; the copies have differed by the p. 63 item for at least sixteen years. Nocedal's host timed out on 2026-10-17, so Wright's copy, the one without the p. 63 item, is the only author-hosted copy still served. Not stated: who added the p. 63 item and why Wright's copy did not receive it; whether corrections reached later printings. Nocedal's second-edition errata web page read 'Errata in the Second Edition [not yet posted]' in 2016 (B011 p. 4).

method_links.note: Numbered public errata, but maintenance stopped in May 2008 and the two hosted copies were never reconciled; the '80 numbered book errata' count holds for Nocedal's copy (B003) only, Wright's copy has 79. Joint voice; keeping public errata is Wright's Heuristic 5, so this fails exclusivity. The Nocedal-specific part of Heuristic 7 stays with the code record (S016, S005, S098).
Step 3 (publish corrections as versioned errata): dated, but two copies with different item numbering, neither naming the other. Joint voice.

transferable: Keep one master errata file and link every host to it; if two copies must exist, put a version line in each that names the other (pp. 1, 5).
Cite an errata item by host and date as well as by number, because the numbering shifts after an insertion: B004 item 12 is not B003 item 12 (p. 1).
Before counting a list's items or dating it, compare the copies' header dates and their archive digests (p. 1).

quotes.text: Corrections to Numerical Optimization, Second Edition Published August 2006 (Last updated May 17, 2008)
Replace the paragraph starting on line 1 and ending on line 10 (that is, “It remains to verify....” through “proof of (ii) is complete”) with the following paragraph:

title: Corrections to Second Printing of Numerical Optimization (first edition; last updated October 2, 2008)
contribution: The authors' joint 91-item corrections to the second printing of the first edition, written as paste-ready LaTeX for the typesetter (p. 1). My grouping: 11 theorem, proof or definition fixes (Theorem 3.4 restated; Theorems 3.5-3.6 and a trust-region hypothesis weakened; a circular Newton proof and Theorem 4.7's constants repaired; the cone and affine-hull definitions), 17 algorithm fixes, 8 exercise or figure fixes and 55 formula, notation or wording fixes; none in Chapters 1, 8 (Quasi-Newton) or 11. Three dated versions exist (Sept 17, 2004: 90 items; Feb 13, 2006: 91; Oct 2, 2008: item 76 itself corrected). Against the first-printing sheet, one fix (book p. 91) was corrected again and one ((5.37)) had to be repeated.
problem_entry: A numbered list of 91 corrections to the first edition's second printing, addressed to the typesetter as LaTeX to paste into the book file; equation labels in the corrected sentences 'may not print, or may print with wrong equation numbers' and show as '??' (pp. 1, 4, 7). No acknowledgement or finder list anywhere (pp. 1-7).
key_idea: What is corrected (my grouping, each item counted once): theorem statements, hypotheses, proofs and definitions 11 (items 3, 4, 5, 15-18, 47, 48, 89, 90); algorithm statements and step rules 17 (8, 12, 22, 27-29, 32, 53-55, 56, 58, 76-77, 82, 83, 85); exercises and figures 8 (13, 35, 75; 37, 38, 71, 87, 88); the other 55 are formulas, signs, indices, notation, wording, cross-references and one reference year (pp. 1-7). By first-edition chapter [B005 pp. 10-19]: Ch. 2: 1, Ch. 3: 5, Ch. 4 (trust region): 12, Ch. 5: 8, Ch. 6: 6, Ch. 7: 6, Ch. 9: 2, Ch. 10: 1, Ch. 12: 8, Ch. 13: 6, Ch. 14: 4, Ch. 15: 3, Ch. 16: 10, Ch. 17: 6, Ch. 18: 10, App. A: 2, references: 1; none in Ch. 1, 8 or 11, and none in the quasi-Newton and limited-memory sections (book pp. 192-234), which the first-printing sheet does correct (book pp. 208, 220, 221; B007 pp. 3-4). Links to the first-printing sheet: book p. 91 line 7 (proof of Theorem 4.7) went from rho_k > 1/2 to 3/4 (B007 p. 2, item 10) and now from 3/4 to 1/4, with the line-6 bound 1/4 -> 1/2 and a factor 2 deleted in (4.44) (items 16-18, pp. 2-3; page images), so the first fix was absorbed and was itself wrong (inference); the (5.37) fix C^-1 b -> C^-T b is listed in both sheets (B007 p. 2; item 21, p. 3), so it had not reached the second printing (inference).
assumptions: Hypotheses and definitions corrected: Theorems 3.5-3.6 need f only twice continuously differentiable, 'not three times' (item 4, p. 1); a trust-region convergence hypothesis on book p. 89 changes from a bounded level set to f bounded below on the level set, '(The formula (4.38) remains the same.)' (item 15, p. 2); Theorem 3.4 restated for any r in ((lambda_n - lambda_1)/(lambda_n + lambda_1), 1) and for all k sufficiently large (item 3, p. 1; page image); the cone needs alpha > 0 instead of alpha >= 0 and the affine-hull definition and example 'are wrong' (items 89-90, p. 7); a rank condition changes from column to row, statement not named (item 73, p. 6).
proof_devices: Item 5 (book p. 53): a Newton local-convergence proof that assumed x_k -> x* is repaired by fixing a radius r with ||inverse Hessian at x_k|| <= 2||inverse Hessian at x*|| for ||x_k - x*|| <= r, choosing ||x_0 - x*|| <= min(r, 1/(2L~)) and arguing inductively to convergence and the quadratic rate (p. 1; page image).

Items 16-18: constants in the proof of Theorem 4.7 (book pp. 90-91): a factor 2 deleted in (4.44), |rho_k - 1| <= 1/2 instead of 1/4, rho_k > 1/4 instead of 3/4 (pp. 2-3; page images); the same line had been changed from 1/2 to 3/4 in the first-printing sheet (B007 p. 2).
Item 48: a missing f(x*) term restored in a second-order chain of inequalities (book p. 346; p. 4).
Item 3: Theorem 3.4's rate statement gains a slightly larger multiplier and an asymptotic proviso (p. 1).
experiments: n/a (no experiments). Two items make numerical statements without data: item 58, 'The algorithm is slightly better if the min with 1 is not performed.' (interior-point step lengths, p. 5); item 87, Exercise 18.2's starting point and solution 'are transposed' (p. 7).
positioning: No finder is named (pp. 1-7), unlike the second-edition list, which thanks three readers (B004 p. 5). One item corrects the year of reference [23] to 1995 (item 91, p. 7).
writing: Each item gives the book page and line (negative lines from the bottom) and the fault, often with tagged replacement text ('Corrected sentence', 'Corrected equation', 'Corrected passage', 'Corrected phrase', 'Corrected fragment') (pp. 1-7). Some items state their reason: '(i.e. gradient not Hessian)' (item 29, p. 3), '(The formula (4.38) remains the same.)' (item 15, p. 2), '(This change is not necessary, but it improves clarity.)' (item 76, p. 6), a performance reason for item 58 (p. 5). Hedges removed: item 31 drops 'minor' from 'minor weakness' and 'slightly' (book p. 141; p. 3); the weakness itself is not quoted. Reading notes (slips in the sheet, not findings): 'to all the proviso' (item 3, p. 1), 'defintion' and 'is a the set' (items 89-90, p. 7), the exponent on [AA^T] printed as 1 in item 88 (p. 7, page image).
limits_future: Three dated versions (my check of Internet Archive CDX listings and the captured PDFs, 2026-10-17): Sept 17, 2004 (captures 2006-01-10 and 2006-02-11; 6 pp., 90 items); Feb 13, 2006 (captures 2006-06-22 to 2007-04-17; 7 pp., 91 items; inserts the book p. 334 item (12.36) as item 45); Oct 2, 2008 = B008 (captures 2008-10-06 and 2018-09-22 to 2024-09-11, same SHA-1 as the local file; item 76's formulas gain the nabla_x they lacked). The works.json note's claim that the 2006-01-10 capture 'has the same items word for word' is wrong: it lacks item 45. B011 p. 3's link label '(updated 2/12/06)' matches the February 2006 version within a day and was not updated after 2008 (capture 2016-05-01). The sheet was kept 2004-2008, and its only update after the second edition appeared (Oct 2008) corrects one of its own items; Oct 2, 2008 is the latest date on any of the book's errata lists read in this increment (B003 p. 1; B004 p. 1; B007 p. 7). Not stated: who found each error; whether the third printing absorbed any item (B011 p. 3 offers the sheet for second and third printings); whether the corrections reached the second edition (body not open; chapters renumbered, e.g. Quasi-Newton is Ch. 8 in the first edition and Ch. 6 in the second [B005 p. 13; B001 p. 9]; no quoted string of B008 recurs in B003, a weak check). Page-only chapter assignments near chapter ends in Ch. 13-18 are approximate: the sheet's book pages run about two pages beyond B005's contents (B005 pp. 15, 18).

method_links.note: Numbered, dated, versioned errata maintained 2004-2008, the last update correcting the sheet's own item 76 (D8). Variant detail: no finder credited, unlike the second-edition list. Joint voice; keeping public errata is Wright's Heuristic 5, so this fails exclusivity.
Step 3: one sheet per printing (B011 p. 3); later sheets correct and repeat earlier fixes (book pp. 91, 118; B007 p. 2). Joint voice.
Weak and joint: item 31 strips 'minor' and 'slightly' from a stated weakness; one item, and the weakness itself was not read (book body not open).

transferable: Write each correction as drop-in replacement text, tagged ('Corrected sentence') and keyed to book page and line, so that the printer can paste it (p. 1).
When a proof does not use a hypothesis, weaken the published statement and say what stays unchanged (items 4, 15; pp. 1-2).
Before correcting a passage, check the previous printing's sheet: the inequality on book p. 91 was changed twice (B007 p. 2; items 17-18, pp. 2-3).
In a new printing's sheet, repeat every fix the reprint missed; the (5.37) correction appears in both sheets (B007 p. 2; item 21, p. 3).
Mark optional changes and changes made for performance as such: 'not necessary, but it improves clarity' (item 76, p. 6); 'slightly better' (item 58, p. 5).
For a local-convergence proof, first fix a neighbourhood in which the inverse Hessian is bounded, then start inside it and argue by induction, rather than assuming convergence (item 5, p. 1).

quotes.text: To make it easier for the typesetter, we have included in many cases an explicit correction of the offending passages, marked by the tag “corrected sentence” or similar, so that he/she can cut-and-paste from the source (latex) file of this document into the latex file for the book.
The theorem needs to be corrected, to include a slightly larger multiplier on the right-hand side of the inequality and to all the proviso that the inequality holds for all k sufficiently large.
